quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. You will find them on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog. High beams will reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions coming up. This sign means a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: In rainy weather, reduce your speed to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes tires to ride up on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to avoid collisions. Do not use it to make slow drivers go faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before it affects your driving?
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: A round sign warns of a railroad crossing. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. What should you do if a driver behind you wants to drive faster?

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
They brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop much faster than regular vehicles. Following too closely is dangerous to you and the motorcyclist. If the rider makes a mistake, you need space and time to avoid a crash.

questions.question: This white sign means you cannot pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must follow the rule shown. This sign means drivers cannot pass other vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with stop signs on all four corners at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time to a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance areas ahead.

questions.question: A traffic light is red, but a police officer directs you to go through without stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.explanation: Police officer directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow what the officer tells you to do.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs your judgment. You need good judgment to drive safely and react to what you see and hear on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events:
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or unusual events. This is called rubbernecking and causes traffic to slow down.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: Use antifreeze washer fluid because:

options.text: Cold fluid can scratch your windshield.
Moisture can cause cold wiper blades to crack.
It keeps the washer fluid from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps the washer fluid from freezing.
questions.explanation: Use antifreeze washer fluid when temperatures may fall below freezing. You need to be able to clean salt, dirt, and slush from your windshield in winter weather.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant in any amount. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces your ability to think clearly and stay alert.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a winding road is ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. You should reduce your speed.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross your path or where traffic lines meet, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to make sure no one is coming.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic next to that broken line may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is an important step in turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: When turning, look to the rear and both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: While driving at night, an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle with your peripheral vision.
